story: At 4:17 on this rainy Tuesday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary is stepping onto pickleball court one to warm up for doubles, while Donna, upbeat as ever, praises him for filing his form and promises a two-hour session on his dink shot before dinner. Over on Magnolia Loop, Hal dutifully checks the mailbox kiosk for any replies from the Architectural Review committee. Back at her house, Rosa is setting out the tablecloth and platters and counting chairs for her four dinner guests and herself, looking determined to get everything just right.
events: Gary (pickleball court 1): Step onto the court and start warming up for doubles
Hal (mailbox kiosk): Check for any Architectural Review committee notices or replies
Rosa (rosa dining table): Set the tablecloth and platters on the table and confirm the chair count for four guests plus me

gary.thought_process: I already told Donna about the form and thanked her, and she's reserving a two-hour slot at the kiosk for doubles practice. No need to repeat myself. Best move is to be a good partner: step up to the court and get on with practice, show I'm on time this go-round. The cart wiring stays on hold until Architectural Review signs off. It's drizzling, but a short shower won't stop an old HVAC man.

parameters.content: Step onto the court and start warming up for doubles

donna.thought_process: Gary just showed up and apologized for being late, and he's confirmed he filed the cart form properly, which keeps me out of trouble with the committee. I already signed us up on the ladder and reserved a two-hour slot at the kiosk last tick, so no need to ask him again. It's time to stop chatting and get him on the court before the shower gets worse. Good practice is how we climb the ladder.

parameters.content: No apology needed, Gary, and good on you for filing that form. I've got us a two-hour slot, so grab a paddle and let's get you working on that dink shot before dinner.

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop, nobody around, and the flamingos are right here. I already counted them at tick 125 and Donna said she trimmed to three. Rather than repeat that, I should handle the Architectural Review matter for Gary's cart — I checked the bulletin board last tick, but a rain shower and an empty street means no distractions. Actually, the mailbox kiosk might hold the committee's reply on cart approvals. Gary followed the rules, Donna complied, so my watchdog duties are mostly satisfied. Check the mailbox for any committee notices, then head to the rec center for the evening.

parameters.content: Check for any Architectural Review committee notices or replies

rosa.thought_process: It's Tuesday afternoon, the shower is keeping everyone indoors, and I'm alone in the house. I've already prepped the make-ahead dishes, counted place settings, checked my shifts, and pulled out the tablecloth and platters. The one loose end is the extra chairs I set aside, since I need to borrow or buy enough seats for four. Gary hasn't given me a firm yes or a dish yet, so I'll check the dining table and confirm the final seating count, then chase Gary when I see him instead of nagging him again.

parameters.content: Set the tablecloth and platters on the table and confirm the chair count for four guests plus me

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
